subject: chemistry
title: Covalent and dative covalent bonding
key_idea: A covalent bond is the strong electrostatic attraction between the nuclei of two atoms and the pair of electrons they share. In a dative covalent bond both electrons come from one atom. Multiple bonds are shorter and stronger than single bonds.

blocks.text: Atoms share electrons to complete their outer shells. This section covers single and multiple covalent bonds and how to draw them.

items.meaning: The strong electrostatic attraction between two nuclei and the shared pair of electrons between them.
A pair of outer electrons that is not used in bonding.

items: A single bond contains one shared pair of electrons. A double bond contains two pairs and a triple bond contains three pairs.
In a diagram a covalent bond is drawn as a line.
Examples are H₂, O₂ (double bond), N₂ (triple bond), Cl₂, HCl, CO₂ (two double bonds), NH₃, CH₄, C₂H₆ and C₂H₄ (a C=C double bond).
Show only the outer electrons, with dots for one atom and crosses for the other.
Overlap the circles where the atoms share a pair.
Show every lone pair, for example two lone pairs on the O atom in H₂O and one on the N atom in NH₃.
Check that each atom, apart from H, has the right number of outer electrons in total.
A covalent bond is the attraction between two nuclei and the shared pair between them.
Multiple bonds contain more than one shared pair.
Draw lone pairs as well as bonding pairs.

blocks.text: In a dative covalent bond (also called a coordinate bond) both electrons in the shared pair come from the same atom. This section covers when one forms.

items: One atom needs a lone pair to give.
The other atom needs an empty orbital to accept it.
Once formed, a dative bond is identical to any other covalent bond.
It is drawn as an arrow pointing from the atom that gives the pair to the atom that receives it.
NH₃ + H⁺ → NH₄⁺. The N atom donates its lone pair to the H⁺ ion, which has an empty orbital.
NH₃ and HCl gases react to form solid NH₄Cl, which contains the NH₄⁺ ion.
In Al₂Cl₆, each Al atom in AlCl₃ has only six outer electrons. A lone pair on a Cl atom of the other molecule forms a dative bond to it, joining two AlCl₃ units together.
In H₃O⁺, an O atom donates a lone pair to H⁺.
In a dative bond both electrons come from one atom.
The donor has a lone pair and the acceptor has an empty orbital.
NH₄⁺ and Al₂Cl₆ are the standard examples.

sections.heading: Expanded octets and up to six electron pairs

blocks.text: Some atoms hold more than eight electrons in their outer shell. This section covers when this happens.

items: Elements in period 3 and below can expand their octet because they have empty d orbitals available.
In PCl₅ the P atom has five bonding pairs, which is ten electrons.
In SF₆ the S atom has six bonding pairs, which is twelve electrons.
In SO₂ the S atom has two double bonds, or one double bond and one dative bond, and a lone pair, so it has more than eight electrons.
Some compounds are odd-electron species. NO has one unpaired electron, so one atom cannot have a full octet.

blocks.text: Diagrams may show up to six electron pairs, bonding and lone, around a central atom.

items: Period 3 elements can have more than eight electrons round the central atom.
PCl₅ and SF₆ are expanded octets.

blocks.text: Bond strength depends on how close the nuclei are and how many electrons are shared. This section covers how to compare bonds.

items.meaning: The distance between the nuclei of two covalently bonded atoms.
The energy needed to break one mole of a particular covalent bond in the gaseous state.

More shared pairs pull the nuclei closer together, so the bond is shorter and stronger.
The larger the average bond enthalpy, the stronger the covalent bond.
A bond with a high bond energy is harder to break, so the molecule is less reactive. N₂ is unreactive because of its very strong triple bond.
A weaker bond, such as the long I–I bond, is easier to break, so molecules with weaker bonds are more reactive.
Between the same two atoms, a shorter bond is a stronger bond.
Bond energy is the energy to break one mole of a bond in the gaseous state.
Strong bonds make a molecule less reactive.

checks.a: The strong electrostatic attraction between the nuclei of two atoms and the shared pair of electrons between them.

checks.q: Explain how a dative covalent bond forms when NH₃ reacts with H⁺.
checks.a: The N atom in NH₃ has a lone pair. It donates both electrons to the H⁺ ion, which has an empty orbital, forming a shared pair.

checks.q: Explain why the N≡N bond is stronger and shorter than the N–N bond.
checks.a: The N≡N bond has three shared pairs and N–N has one. More shared electrons pull the nuclei closer together, giving a shorter bond that needs more energy to break.

items: Use bond energy values together with bond length to compare the reactivity of covalent molecules.
Know the molecules by name and be able to describe the bonding in each: H₂, O₂, N₂, Cl₂, HCl, CO₂, NH₃, CH₄, C₂H₆ and C₂H₄.
Know that SO₂, PCl₅ and SF₆ have expanded octets, and that NH₃ and HCl form NH₄⁺ by coordinate bonding.
